title: ModTheSpire2
description:
A pre-launch mod selector and in-game companion manager for Slay the Spire 2.

GitHub:
https://github.com/grassdog0/MTS2

Features:
- Native Windows launcher with no extra runtime install.
- Choose vanilla or selected mods before the game starts.
- Dependency-aware mod list: dependent mods are shown under required mods and cannot be selected until dependencies are selected.
- Compatible with standard mod JSON files and Workshop mods that only provide mod_manifest.json.
- Custom load order with Move Up, Move Down, numeric order entry, Save Order, Reset Order, and named order profiles.
- Saved enabled-mod selections, so a one-time Vanilla launch does not erase your normal mod setup.
- In-game ModTheSpire2 management button on the game's Mod Settings page.
- Conservative Hot-Apply section for config/utility mods only; DLL/PCK/UI/gameplay mods remain Restart Required.
- Safe Close and Open Launcher flow to avoid running two game instances at once.
- settings.save backups before ModTheSpire2 writes mod settings.

Important:
Steam Workshop cannot change your Steam launch options automatically. To show ModTheSpire2 every time you press Play, set your Slay the Spire 2 launch option to:

"<path to ModTheSpire2Launcher.exe>" -- %command%

The in-game Close and Open Launcher dialog includes a copy button for this launch option.
changeNote:
Version 0.4.0
- Added dependency-aware launcher ordering and selection.
- Added custom load order saving, numeric order entry, and named order profiles.
- Added saved enabled-mod selections separate from one-time Vanilla launch.
- Corrected hot-apply classification: ModTheSpire2 itself is restart-required because it patches game UI.
- Added compatibility for Workshop mods that use mod_manifest.json, including Act 4 Heart / Act4Heart.
- Removed unsafe standalone Open Launcher flow from the in-game overlay.
- Kept Copy Launch Option only inside the safe Close and Open Launcher confirmation dialog.
- Added launcher self-tests and package verification for load order, dependencies, saved enabled selections, and manifest compatibility.
